transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE); Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE); Maya Rios (Asterion CTO); Liam Chen (Principal ML Eng); Priya Nair (Infra); Noah Park (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. primary concerns: p95 latency with streaming, concurrency at burst, cost tradeoffs, KV cache cold/warm, security (VPC/KMS).

00:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): ok everyone greet, thanks for joining, quick agenda, want to figure out your p95 targets and burst patterns so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pilot.
00:18 Maya (Asterion): yeah thanks, we run a realtime insights chat in our product, typical responses are 60-400 tokens, mostly 80-150 tokens, and we need p95 under 800ms for short answers and under 2s for streaming 300 token responses.
00:34 Liam: to add, spikes are big — approx 200-300 concurrent users during peak events, but those users often open 4-6 streams each in 30s bursts, so token/sec bursts matter.
00:50 Daniel (Redwood SE): ok makes sense. are those concurrent numbers per region? and do you have average tokens/sec per stream we can use?
00:59 Noah: primarily US-east, but we also have EU customers in EMEA. tokens/sec per stream average ~18-25, peak up to 60 for some synth workloads.
01:15 Priya: we have strict data residency and audit needs; SOC2 in progress, and anything with private data must be behind our VPC for the pilot.
01:30 Sofia: good, so we're hearing p95 targets ~800ms short, 2s for longer streaming. concurrency ~300 simultaneous streams in peak, tokens/sec bursts up to ~60. ok we can work with that.
02:02 Maya: curious on cold start — we've seen big p95 hits on cold KV cache. how does Redwood handle KV warmup and prefix caching?
02:18 Daniel: Redwood runtime has automatic KV caching and prefix reuse, but cold start depends on resident cache and model variant. for hosted, we recommend keepalive/long-lived workers for streaming use-cases to keep KV hot. there is also an option to pin model shards in Dedicated.
02:40 Liam: and for quantized models — do we lose throughput or is latency actually better? we've historically seen A100 fp16 run faster but H100 with quantization behaves differently.
02:55 Daniel: short answer: it depends. int8 quant can reduce memory and improve concurrency but single-stream latency can impact depending on kernel choices. on H100 we see good streaming latency with q4_0 for many Llama-family models. we should bench your model.
03:22 Maya: ok benching is important. we can provide a 24-hour trace and a few sample prompts for profiling.
03:35 Sofia: perfect, we'll include microbench (p95 token latency), macrobench (overall tokens/sec), and cold-start sims.
03:52 Noah: on networking: if we do private, expect to negotiate cross-account VPC peering and a bastion. latency within VPC should be fine but egress to Redwood control plane needs TLS + SST — sorry SAML for auth.
04:10 Priya: also need KMS integration for key wrapping, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. you mentioned Redwood Private supports HSM/KMS?
04:22 Daniel: yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log shipping. our default is envelope encryption with customer keys for on-prem.
04:38 Maya: what about fallback? if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can Redwood fallback to hosted? we want graceful degradation, not 503s.
04:52 Sofia: yes, smart routing can failover to compatible model variants in hosted, but you'd need an explicit policy to allow cross-tenancy fallback. customers often allow a lower-cost hosted variant as a fallback.
05:12 Liam: cost tradeoffs — curious how batching affects p95. we've noticed aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latencies. thoughts?
05:28 Daniel: continuous batching is workload-aware. for streaming, we keep smaller micro-batches to preserve p95. Dedicated lets you control batch thresholds. we can provide suggested thresholds after a profiler run.
05:45 Maya: good. can you talk about warm vs cold p95 numbers you typically observe? ballpark numbers for a 7B-ish model on H100 for streaming: warm p95 ~200-350ms per chunk, cold p95 up to 1.5x-2x?
06:05 Daniel: that's a reasonable ballpark. warm streaming chunk p95 ~150-400ms depending on token size and kernel. cold can be 800ms-1.2s on top of that for initial KV load, especially if the request triggers model load. pinning solves a lot.
06:30 Sofia: given your constraints (data residency), seems Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is likely. Hosted could be for non-sensitive flows or fallback. what would success look like for your team?
06:45 Maya: success = <800ms p95 for under-150-token responses, <2s for 300-token streams, <5% error rate during bursts, and full audit logs in our SIEM. Pilot needs to run for 3 months.
07:05 Sofia: ok pilot scope noted. question for you — do you have GPU preferences? A100 vs H100?
07:12 Liam: we currently use A100 in prod for training. infra team prefers H100 for inference if perf gains are clear. cost uplift is a concern.
07:22 Daniel: we can show comparative benchmarks. sometimes H100 yields lower latency for large batch workloads; for conversational streaming with small batches, difference is model-dependent.
07:40 Noah: regarding concurrency: if we need to support 300 streams with 20 tokens/sec and avg 120 tokens per response, that's... math... about 720k tokens per minute at peak — does that map to units you price on?
07:58 Sofia: yes we price per-token on hosted, and dedicated is capacity-based. we'll map your sample traces to tokens-per-minute and recommend committed capacity. also there are autoscale burst policies.
08:20 Maya: can we do a bench with our trace that simulates cold start and warm state?
08:28 Daniel: absolutely. ideal plan: you share trace -> we run 3 sims (cold, warm, and mixed bursts) on Hosted H100 and Dedicated pool (pinned model) and send a report with p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
08:44 Priya: one more — TLS termination and where logs are stored. we need to ensure logs don't contain PII.
08:52 Daniel: we can redact by default and ship audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle. Private keeps logs in your control.
09:07 Sofia: timeline: if you give traces by Dec 22, we can return a bench report by Dec 28 and propose pilot pricing the week after. sound ok?
09:18 Maya: yes that works.

[discussion continues — transcript shows technical digressions and clarifications, occasional crosstalk and imperfect transcription]

20:10 Liam: in our last system we saw p95 jump when KV cache evicted on scale-down, any suggestions?
20:25 Daniel: avoid scale-down during peak; use grace periods. Dedicated reserved pools help. we also recommend warmup scripts that replay recent context to populate KV.
21:05 Priya: do you surface token-level cost in the console? our finance team will ask for per-route cost views.
21:18 Sofia: yes console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. we can also add an export for your finance team.
22:40 Maya: security checklist — SSO, SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, SOC2. do you have a security pack?
22:55 Daniel: we have an enterprise security pack (SOC2 reports, audit pipeline), we can send the security pack PDF and SOC2 artifact.
24:01 Noah: also, we sometimes need deterministic rollbacks for model regressions. does Redwood support rollouts and automatic fallback?
24:12 Daniel: yes, rollout policies and automatic fallback to previous model variants or hosted compat are built in. you can set canary percentages and automatic rollback triggers on quality regressions.
25:05 Maya: would you recommend starting on Hosted pilot or Dedicated?
25:18 Sofia: because of your data residency and VPC constraints, I'd recommend a Dedicated pilot with VPC peering or Private if you require full on-prem. Dedicated is faster to stand up and gives predictable throughput.
25:35 Liam: big question — how do you quantify p95 improvements vs cost for us?
25:45 Daniel: we'll produce a delta report: p95 vs tokens/sec vs cost across Hosted H100, Dedicated pooled instances (A100/H100), and Private (on-prem). you'll get charts and recommended batch/config settings.
26:12 Maya: ok let's confirm next steps and owners.
26:20 Sofia: recap: Daniel runs bench sims; Maya/Liam provide traces; Sofia sends pricing; Noah shares network/VPC details. timeline dec 18/20/22/23 for deliverables.
26:40 Maya: sounds good.
26:50 Speaker 1: (inaudible) thanks everyone.
27:05 Sofia: one last note — we sometimes suggest hybrid routing: keep hot-user flows on Dedicated and cold async flows on Hosted to save money. possible if you allow fallback.
27:28 Priya: that seems appealing.
27:45 Liam: ok thanks, we'll assemble traces and SSO details.
28:00 Sofia: I'll follow up in email with the benchmark template and a calendar invite for the profiling session.
28:14 Maya: thanks much.
28:20 Meeting close

-- End of transcript (note: transcript contains typical automated disfluencies and mislabels)
